earlier_failures: First identity test expected a permission-display prefix absent from the existing RuntimeError Display. Implementation already returned the redacted message; assertion corrected.
First HTTP harness expected 403 for an unknown/encoded static route. Axum returned 404; route-appropriate refusal expectations corrected.

Second HTTP harness expected immediate NeedsRecovery after a fixture panic. Actual durable state correctly retained InFlight; explicit reentry marks uncertainty with no new model/effect. Harness corrected and no-write reentry asserted.

First separate-process probe failed startup on both backends: the example supplied only max_cost_micros in a RunLimits object whose other fields are required. Source examples now contain complete bounded limits, and the final harness uses those source configs. Original startup logs/configs are retained.
limits: SQL identities and actual loopback transport are real. Models in these service/auth checks are explicitly offline/fixtures, not native API effectiveness, fees or latency evidence.
Actual fsynced test writes exercise exact approval, authenticated actors and lost-result reconciliation. They do not make external effects exactly-once.
Project Application journals remain file-backed; no SQL Application selection, durable quota/queue/distributed-worker or service load acceptance.
Project members share project run/workflow/session history. Fixed single-operator memory config is refused; user-private memory service endpoints are disabled.
Host SQL/SDK administration is trusted. No identity-administration REST endpoint, hosted login provider, TLS provisioning or browser multi-user UI is implemented.
Revocation/downgrade affects subsequent authorization, not retroactive cancellation of already-authorized work. Role-specific host-tool grants remain a future refinement.
Catalog bounded to 1024 users/4096 tokens/20000 audit events and record byte cap; no automatic audit/token compaction.
Process probes passed ten controls per backend, then killed only their owned idle servers. Private bearer files/database credentials and database files are excluded from this source artifact.
No coordinated SQL-identity plus project-files backup, production deployment/load acceptance, entire-goal completion, source publication or framework-ranking claim.
